contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-address-element-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-address-element-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-address-element.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/address-element`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/address-element, the November 7 capture describes an Address Element for complete in-app billing and shipping addresses and links the iOS, Android and React Native variants. It contains no per-platform setup or payment flow (new raw lines 5-15). The April 22 capture describes the embeddable UI and full billing use such as tax. All three expanded overviews list 236 regional address formats including right-to-left, autocomplete, prefill if a customer address is already saved, Appearance API customization, and web/mobile availability. The listed integration and data-passing partners are iOS Payment Sheet and Payment Element, and Android and React Native Payment Element and Link (old raw lines 8-26, old raw lines 28-46, old raw lines 48-66). source-stripe-inapp-address-element.md captures the April component and common feature list. Its blanket parity and Payment Sheet pairing language need platform qualification, and the separate Collect addresses guide is already represented in the wiki. Collecting or prefilling an address is UI state; the distinct implementation guide documents optional shipping-details configuration and PaymentIntent.shipping on confirmation with those details populated (raw/stripe-inapp-collect-addresses-2025.md:136-148,524-532,711-717).
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/address-element, the capture changes are navigation and presentation. November indexes the three mobile variants and no longer embeds their April bodies, screenshots or Collect addresses links. It supplies no product-level change or withdrawal evidence. Keep the April feature list, 236 formats including RTL, saved-address prerequisite for prefill, Appearance API, named integration pairs, and guide routes dated in source-stripe-inapp-address-element.md (old raw lines 8-26, old raw lines 28-66, new raw lines 5-15). Correct the stale guide status and link this overview and source-stripe-inapp-collect-addresses.md in both directions through the in-app concept. The companion’s separately captured November index lists iOS UIKit, iOS SwiftUI, Android and React Native. This overview lists three platform links. Keep the companion’s detailed implementation dated to April (raw/stripe-payments-mobile-collect-addresses-2026-11-07.md:5-16, wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-collect-addresses.md:11-24,128-136). The April companion guide documents optional passing of the collected shipping address through PaymentSheet.Configuration.shippingDetails on iOS and Android and defaultShippingDetails on React Native. These settings prefill billing and display the option to reuse the shipping address as billing. With the configured details populated, PaymentIntent.shipping is documented when the intent is confirmed (raw/stripe-inapp-collect-addresses-2025.md:136-148,524-532,711-717). The separate web route combines address and payment data on confirmation when the components share the same Stripe.js Elements instance (wiki/concepts/stripe-address-element.md:27-41). iOS autocomplete is on by default. Android autocomplete, including React Native on Android, requires the Google Places SDK and an API key (raw/stripe-inapp-collect-addresses-2025.md:12-18,457-469,644-656). Collection or a UI callback does not establish payment success or an automatic server update, and the November overview establishes no SDK or REST API version, payment outcome, or measured conversion improvement.
